script.base: Spread, total, and implied team totals were not saved, so this script is inferred only from the three-game sheet, not from a market number. WAS should be the side that moves the ball: IND blitzes only 23% and the WAS QB is +0.17 EPA/dropback when not blitzed (vs -0.04 when blitzed, n=25), while IND allows 5.08 YPC, 10 runs of 10+, and 10.74 YPA in the middle. IND's offense stays Taylor-led on the ground (66 carries, 258 yards) into a sturdier WAS front (4.00 YPC, 5 runs of 10+), with Jones inefficient overall (EPA -0.20 unblitzed, -0.03 vs blitz, n=32) against a 47% WAS blitz that pushes IND toward short throws rather than a vertical shootout.
script.flip1: IND gets ahead on Taylor's 22-carry pace, the game becomes a clock-kill, and WAS — already a committee (Croskey-Merritt 47 carries, White 22, Daniels 12) — abandons the run so Diggs and McLaurin (22 targets each) absorb a pass-heavy chase.
script.flip2: The WAS 47% blitz does not speed Jones up and IND attacks the middle, where WAS allows 12.29 YPA on 21 attempts and 11 passes of 20+ on 107 throws; Downs' 281 air yards connect and the short-throw cap on Warren breaks.

Re-run if a late scratch hits Taylor, Downs, Warren, or the WAS backfield.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man-vs-zone charting are not in the pack. Location splits are the only proxy: WAS allows 5.29 YPA left (35 att), 12.29 middle (21 att), 9.39 right (46 att). IND allows 8.61 left (31), 10.74 middle (23), 8.16 right (44).
matchup.pressure: No pressure rate in the pack. WAS blitzes 47%; IND QB EPA is -0.03 vs blitz (n=32) and -0.20 with no blitz, so Jones is less bad when blitzed, which fits getting the ball out short. WAS QB EPA is -0.04 vs blitz (n=25) and +0.17 with no blitz, and IND blitzes only 23%, so WAS is likely to see the look it handles.
matchup.bleeds: WAS bleeds the middle (12.29 YPA) and has allowed 11 passes of 20+ on 107 attempts; the left side is a wall at 5.29. WAS run defense is the sturdy unit: 4.00 YPC and only 5 runs of 10+. IND bleeds the run (5.08 YPC, 10 runs of 10+) and the middle (10.74 YPA), with 10 passes of 20+ on 105 attempts.
matchup.overlap: IND's primary target is Josh Downs (24 targets, 281 air yards). That downfield diet overlaps WAS's middle bleed and 11 explosives allowed, but the 47% blitz is the counterweight and the left side is not a bleed — overlap is unconfirmed without alignment charting. Warren (22 targets, 38 air yards) does not attack that middle bleed; he is the underneath valve the blitz would feed. WAS co-primaries Diggs and McLaurin (22 targets each; McLaurin 286 air, Diggs 188) overlap IND's middle bleed and a 23% blitz that does not punish WAS's +0.17 unblitzed EPA. Taylor's 66 carries do not overlap a run-defense bleed.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Warren under 58.5 is the edge because the number is pricing normal efficiency on his 7.3 targets a game (about 8 yards per target to clear), but his role is a dump-off: 89 yards on 22 targets with only 38 air yards, so 4.0 yards per target is the job, not a cold streak, and a 47% WAS blitz adds more of those same short targets rather than the downfield yards needed to double his 29.7-yard average.
edge_players.must_be_true: He keeps the short-area role (about 1.7 air yards per target), plays his normal snap share, and stays active — no injury tag or inactive list is in the pack, so this is script-stable rather than script-dependent, and it still holds if IND falls behind and checkdowns increase.
edge_players.kills_it: One blitz bust or YAC explosive (a 35-40 yard catch) or a role change where Downs is taken away and Warren's targets jump with real after-catch yards; 10 targets at even 6 yards per target is still only 60, so it takes a true outlier, not a modest volume bump.

data_check.notes: No projection model, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig is in the pack, so this is a rate check only and cannot be sized. Warren's 29.7 yards/game and 38 air yards agree with under 58.5 by a wide margin; even a blitz-driven bump to 10 targets at his 4.0 yards/target is about 40, still under. No model probability near 70% to distrust. Price on this rung is +nan, so there is no sharp number to agree or disagree with. Considered and dropped, not flagged: Taylor rush under 92.5 (86/game and 22 carries times WAS 4.00 YPC is about 88, but the cushion is noise and flip 1 kills it); Croskey-Merritt rush over 61 (IND's 5.08 YPC is the matchup read, but it is a lean and his 47.3-yard mean disagrees, so step 8 says drop); Downs over 72 (middle-bleed overlap, but 62-yard mean disagrees and alignment is uncharted). Okonkwo under 29.5 and Dyami Brown under 11.5 were not used: both are priced near a pick'em (-116/-113.5 and -113/-115) despite 5.3 and 7 yards per game, which may be news this pack does not have.

market_rung_price: tylerwarren recyds under 58.5, main line, price not in pack (+nan). No alt rung saved. Do not invent a short-priced alt. Only rushyds/recyds/rushrecyds considered; no passing yards, TDs, or receptions.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and Warren under 58.5 lost. WAS blitzed 47%, Jones got the ball out, and one busted checkdown turned into a 40-yard YAC play that the 38-air-yard sample said was unlikely but a receiving-yards under always allows. Or the missing injury report had Downs limited, Warren's 22 targets became 12 in one game with actual yards after the catch, and 58.5 — the book's efficiency regression, not a sleepy number — was the right projection all along. The counter is a one-play spike, not a role the sheet supports, so the read still beats the counter, but it is the way this leg dies.
slip_story: Single-leg IND short-game cap, not a shootout stack and not a clock-kill stack. Warren under wins in the base script (WAS blitz, Jones dumping underneath, Warren staying a 4-yards-per-target valve) and also in flip 1 if IND leads and the passing game stays short. It loses with flip 2 only if the explosive is his, not Downs'. No second leg from the available rush/rec/rush-rec board survived the pre-mortem without needing the opposite script or fading a number the sheet does not beat. Do not pair him with Downs, Diggs, or Taylor overs.
